Algebra 1 | Quarter 2 | Unit 4: Linear Equations and Functions

From Trailhead to Summit

Where does the model make sense?

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 8–9
Topic
Domain and Range
Standards
HSF-IF.A.1, HSF-IF.B.5, HSF-IF.A.2

Students find domain and range from graphs, tables and sets of pairs, choose reasonable domains for real models, and write them with inequalities and interval notation.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Find the domain and range from a graph, a table or a set of ordered pairs.
  • Choose a reasonable domain and range for a real-world model.
  • Write domain and range using inequalities and interval notation.
  • Tell the difference between a discrete and a continuous domain.

3Essential question

A trail equation can be evaluated anywhere. Why does it only make sense on part of the number line?

5MTB connection

The equation for a climb can be evaluated at d = −3000 or d = 20000, but the trail doesn’t exist there. The domain is the part of the model that matches the real trail: trailhead to summit.

Choosing the domain is a modelling decision, and stating it is what stops a model from making silly predictions.

The mathOn the trail
DomainTrailhead to summit
RangeLowest to highest elevation on the section
Discrete domainNumber of laps or runs
Continuous domainDistance or time
